summary: Fourteen days of closed-loop data show good CGM coverage and a reasonable aggregate time-in-range, but with recurring severe hypoglycemia clusters, recurring severe hyperglycemia clusters, and high glucose variability. No carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the package, so meal effects, basal adequacy, carb ratio adequacy, and automation compensation cannot be separated from one another with confidence. Dynamic ISF appears to be the dominant real-time sensitivity mechanism rather than the flat profile ISF value, and one severe event shows the automation's maximum corrective rate being capped by a safety multiplier tied to a low afternoon basal segment. Given these unresolved, competing explanations, this analysis withholds profile and automation parameter changes and instead prioritizes establishing carbohydrate logging and sequential safety verification before any settings are adjusted.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is excellent (98.7 percent, 5-minute cadence, largest gap 65 minutes, no duplicates or invalid entries). Profile fields are fully populated. Zero carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the 14-day period. Loop status telemetry is only a 24-item representative sample out of 6214 total device statuses.
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.data_quality; treatment_summary; aaps_profile fields; representative_events Profile Switch on 2026-08-13.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data at all; only a small representative sample of device statuses; residual ambiguity about which profile configuration applied before the 2026-08-13 profile switch, resolved per instruction by treating the current profile as authoritative for the full period.

analysis_steps.findings: Aggregate time in range is 86.0 percent with 8.9 percent above range and 5.1 percent below range; coefficient of variation is 32.6 percent. Severe hypoglycemia clusters occurred on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21 (as low as 41-42 mg/dL). Severe hyperglycemia clusters occurred on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18 (up to 293 mg/dL). A pump occlusion and pump error were logged on 2026-08-19, and uploader and pump battery declined sharply near the end of the period, coinciding with increased volatility on 2026-08-19 to 2026-08-21.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary; daily_glucose; glucose_extremes; representative_events Announcements; representative_loop_statuses battery fields.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data to separate meal-driven from correction-driven glucose rises; device reliability issues near period end are a plausible confound for that window's volatility.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight and early morning hours (00:00-04:00 local) show a recurring low-glucose signal, most pronounced at hour 1 local (18.5 percent time below range). The dawn window (05:00-07:00) performs well. From late morning through mid-afternoon (10:00-16:00 local), time above range rises progressively to a peak at hour 15 local (32.1 percent), coinciding with the basal segment dropping to its daily minimum (0.5 U/h at 16:00). Evening hours show glucose falling from afternoon highs into renewed time-below-range. Several relaxed temporary targets (135 mg/dL) were active during parts of the period and were not time-bounded precisely enough to fully re-baseline the hourly statistics.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local; aaps_profile.basal_segments; aaps_profile.target_segments; representative_events Temporary Target entries; therapy_response_windows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data to separate meal effects from basal effects in the 10:00-16:00 window; imprecise temporary-target windows relative to hourly aggregates; cannot yet confirm whether overnight and evening time-below-range reflects basal dosing or trailing insulin-on-board from daytime corrections.

analysis_steps.findings: The profile declares a single flat ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit, but the dynamically applied sensitivity in loop status samples ranged from about 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit, a more than fourfold spread, indicating dynamic ISF is the dominant real-time lever rather than the static profile value. The 16:00 carb ratio segment (10.5 g/U, the most aggressive of the day) coincides with the worst time-above-range window identified in basal_targets, which is consistent with either an unlogged larger meal, a basal insufficiency, or delayed automation response, and cannot be distinguished with current data. Insulin-on-board tails (10-hour duration of insulin action) both support and contradict the evening low-glucose hypothesis in different therapy-response windows, so the duration of insulin action cannot yet be judged as too long or too short.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.isf_segments; aaps_profile.carb_ratio_segments; aaps_profile.dia_hours; representative_loop_statuses variable_sens and reason strings; therapy_response_windows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate entries exist anywhere, which fundamentally limits carb ratio validation to indirect inference; the dynamic ISF engine makes the static profile ISF value largely non-diagnostic on its own.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and, because carbohydrates were never logged, essentially all supplemental microbolus activity is UAM-driven with carbohydrates-on-board consistently at zero; no duplicate carbohydrate-on-board counting was observed. Supplemental microbolusing is enabled during temporary targets but not during high temporary targets; at least one checked severe hyperglycemia event (2026-08-18) shows supplemental microbolusing was active outside any temporary-target window, so this interaction is not confirmed as causal for that event. Delivery interval and duration caps for standard and unannounced-meal microbolusing are internally consistent with each other.
analysis_steps.evidence: representative_loop_statuses reason strings; representative_events Temporary Target entries; treatment_summary carb_entries value of zero.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The exact suppression behavior for high temporary targets in this build cannot be confirmed from the package; only a small sample of device statuses is available to check specific windows.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled while dynamic sensitivity is enabled, which is a coherent deliberate configuration rather than a conflict; sensitivity ratio values near 1 are correctly interpreted as neutral output, not as evidence Autosens is disabled or malfunctioning. The applied dynamic sensitivity tightened appropriately during the worst hyperglycemia events and loosened during lower-glucose periods, suggesting automation is actively compensating for underlying profile gaps rather than malfunctioning. During the 2026-08-14 severe hyperglycemia event, the loop's calculated insulin requirement exceeded the maximum safe basal rate, which is mathematically tied to the low 16:00 basal segment through the current basal safety multiplier; this shows a profile basal magnitude can constrain the automation's maximum emergency response, competing with an unlogged-meal explanation for the same event. Maximum insulin-on-board limit is far above any observed insulin-on-board and does not appear to be an active constraint.
analysis_steps.evidence: representative_loop_statuses variable_sens, sensitivity_ratio, enacted versus suggested rate and maxSafeBasal fields; aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings safety multiplier and max IOB fields.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Only a small sample of device statuses is available, so the frequency of the maximum safe basal ceiling being reached across the full period is unknown; the relative contribution of basal-ceiling capping versus unlogged meals to the afternoon pattern cannot be quantified.

analysis_steps.findings: No prebolus timing or immediate bolus percentage is declared anywhere in aaps_profile.analysis_context.meal_strategies, which is an empty list, and no meal-tagged bolus events exist in telemetry to measure timing against; all sampled treatments are temporary basal or correction bolus events. Two recurring response patterns are visible in correction-bolus response windows: a sustained or renewed glucose rise for two to six hours after a correction on several dates, and a large-correction overshoot into hypoglycemia or near-hypoglycemia within two to four hours on other dates, with one instance directly correlating to a previously flagged severe hypoglycemia cluster on 2026-08-14.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No declared meal-bolus strategy exists to compare against telemetry; without carbohydrate logging the two observed response patterns cannot be attributed specifically to meal timing, carb ratio, insulin-on-board stacking, or automation behavior.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended carbohydrate entries total zero for the entire period, with no average extended-carb duration available. No e-carb amount, start offset, or duration exists to evaluate, and no absorption-time behavior can be validated against real intake.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of carbohydrate and extended-carb logging blocks any assessment of absorption model settings against observed behavior.

analysis_steps.findings: The recurring afternoon hyperglycemia pattern and the recurring evening and overnight hypoglycemia pattern each have multiple plausible, unresolved explanations spanning basal magnitude, carb ratio, dynamic ISF, unlogged meals, insulin-on-board stacking, and an automation safety ceiling tied to basal magnitude. No single cause can be isolated with the available data because carbohydrate intake was never logged. The safest sequence is to first establish carbohydrate logging and monitor the already-identified severe hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia clusters, then reassess basal and automation interactions with the added meal context, and only then consider bolus-strategy refinements, changing one dependent setting at a time.
analysis_steps.evidence: Consolidated findings from data_quality through meal_ecarbs_absorption steps above.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of carbohydrate logging is the single largest gap constraining every downstream inference in this analysis.

strengths: CGM data coverage is excellent (98.7 percent) with stable 5-minute cadence, supporting reliable pattern detection.
Aggregate time in range (86.0 percent) is reasonable and the dawn window (05:00-07:00 local) shows consistently strong control.

Automation's applied sensitivity appears to tighten and loosen in the same direction as observed glucose severity, suggesting the dynamic sensitivity engine is responding appropriately rather than malfunctioning.
Many loop status samples during falling or low glucose show the system correctly suspending or reducing temporary basal delivery rather than continuing to dose.
issues: Recurring severe hypoglycemia clusters on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21, reaching as low as 41-42 mg/dL.
Recurring severe hyperglycemia clusters on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18, reaching up to 293 mg/dL.
Elevated glucose variability (coefficient of variation 32.6 percent) alongside a below-range time percentage (5.1 percent) above typical targets.
Complete absence of carbohydrate logging throughout the 14-day period, which blocks separation of meal effects from basal, carb ratio, insulin sensitivity, and automation effects.

One severe hyperglycemia event (2026-08-14) shows the automation's calculated insulin requirement exceeding the maximum safe basal rate, which is mathematically tied to a low afternoon basal segment through the current basal safety multiplier.
Declining pump and uploader battery together with a logged pump occlusion and pump error near the end of the period coincide with increased glucose volatility in that window.

recommendations.title: Begin logging carbohydrate intake to resolve competing explanations
recommendations.description: No carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the 14-day package, which prevents distinguishing meal-driven glucose excursions from basal, carb ratio, insulin sensitivity, or automation-driven excursions. This is the single change most likely to improve the reliability of every other finding in this analysis.

suggested_change.detail: Log approximate carbohydrate grams and timestamps for representative meals, especially around the 12:00-16:00 local window and evening meals, without changing any delivery settings yet.

recommendations.title: Review recurring severe hypoglycemia clusters with a care team before any setting change
recommendations.description: Severe hypoglycemia clusters on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21 reached 41-42 mg/dL. The cause is not yet separable between insulin-on-board stacking from the 10-hour duration of insulin action, basal magnitude, and unlogged meals.

suggested_change.detail: Discuss the specific dated hypoglycemia events with a care team before adjusting basal, duration of insulin action, or correction-bolus behavior.

recommendations.title: Treat the afternoon basal-automation interaction as a dependency, not an isolated basal issue
recommendations.description: The automation's maximum corrective rate during the 2026-08-14 severe hyperglycemia event was constrained by the current basal safety multiplier applied to the low 16:00 basal segment. Changing the basal segment and the safety multiplier together would make it impossible to attribute future improvement or harm to either change.

suggested_change.detail: Add carbohydrate context first, then re-evaluate this specific afternoon window in isolation before considering either the basal segment or the safety multiplier.

recommendations.title: Monitor, rather than change, the temporary-target and high-temporary-target interaction
recommendations.description: Supplemental microbolusing is enabled during temporary targets but not during high temporary targets. At least one checked severe hyperglycemia event was not explained by this interaction, so it remains an unconfirmed, low-certainty hypothesis.

suggested_change.detail: Note glucose behavior during future temporary-target windows, particularly any that might be classified as high, before considering a change to this setting.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current basal segments unchanged, including the 16:00 segment implicated in the afternoon hyperglycemia pattern and the automation safety-ceiling interaction, until carbohydrate context is available to separate meal effects from basal effects.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The afternoon hyperglycemia pattern (10:00-16:00 local) and the automation safety-ceiling interaction observed on 2026-08-14 are each explainable by unlogged meals, carb ratio adequacy, dynamic sensitivity behavior, or basal magnitude, and the available data does not allow these explanations to be separated. Changing basal now risks correcting the wrong variable.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After carbohydrate logging begins, review whether the 12:00-16:00 local hyperglycemia pattern persists on days without large logged meals in that window; if it does, revisit the 16:00 basal segment and its safety-multiplier interaction as an isolated next step.

Continue relying on that mechanism for now, but treat it as a temporary fallback rather than an intentional prebolus or bolus-percentage strategy, since it cannot be evaluated for adequacy without carbohydrate data.

implementation_steps: Begin logging approximate carbohydrate grams and timestamps for representative meals without changing any current delivery settings.
Continue monitoring the previously identified severe hypoglycemia clusters and severe hyperglycemia clusters and discuss them with a care team before any setting change.

After a period of carbohydrate logging, reassess the 12:00-16:00 local hyperglycemia pattern and the 2026-08-14 automation safety-ceiling event to determine whether they persist on days without large logged meals.

If the afternoon pattern persists despite adequate meal coverage, evaluate the 16:00 basal segment in isolation before considering the basal safety multiplier or any other dependent automation setting.
Make any future change one setting at a time and monitor glucose closely afterward before introducing a second change.
education: Dynamic ISF adjusts insulin sensitivity in real time and can differ substantially from the flat profile ISF value; large swings in applied sensitivity do not necessarily indicate a problem with the static profile setting.

Unannounced-meal supplementation (UAM) responds to detected glucose deviations even when no carbohydrates are logged, which is why carbohydrates-on-board can remain at zero throughout a period that still shows meal-like glucose responses.

A long duration of insulin action means correction boluses can continue lowering glucose for several hours, which can either resolve a high safely or contribute to a later low depending on timing of subsequent doses.

Automation safety multipliers tie the maximum emergency delivery rate to the current basal segment, so a low basal segment can limit how aggressively the system responds to a severe high even when the algorithm calculates a larger need.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; TuneMyBG does not provide medical advice and prepares data for review only.
Independently verify every proposed change with a care team, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely after each change.
The recurring severe hypoglycemia clusters identified in this analysis (as low as 41-42 mg/dL) warrant care team review before any profile or automation setting is modified.
Do not change dependent insulin-delivery settings, such as a basal segment and its associated safety multiplier, at the same time.
